gbm_population_evidence.quote: Pilot Study of Navigated Focused Ultrasound and Pembrolizumab in the Treatment of Recurrent WHO Grade 4 IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma With Mismatch Repair Deficiency

candidate_evidence.quote: Pembrolizumab along with focused ultrasound sonication following surgery for recurrent glioblastoma.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: 6-8 patients with recurrent glioblastoma and identified mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency will be administered pembrolizumab

role_evidence.quote: Treatment dosing will be 200mg of pembrolizumab every three weeks for up to six months or until disease progression, whichever occurs first.
following microbubble (Bracco Imaging, SonoVue® or Lumason®; 0.1 mL/Kg; maximum 4.8 mL) administration on a 2-minute schedule.

agents.drug_class_hint: ultrasound contrast microbubbles used with focused ultrasound

source_quote.quote: MMR deficiencies confirmed per standard of care immunohistochemical analysis or Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) of the patient's surgical sample from the time of initial GBM diagnosis or recurrence.
Patient previously diagnosed with WHO grade 4 IDH-wildtype GBM, determined through genomic and/or histopathological analysis.
To evaluate levels of baseline tumor markers related to immune and genetic repair function, including PD-L1, microsatellite instability (MSI), and tumor mutational burden (TMB).
